Overview AI launches OV Spark inspection cameras with an onboard assistant

Ten inspection tools and the Sparky assistant help configure checks, with on-device production inspection and an early deployment at MEC.

The Robot Report ↗6 October 2026English editorial summary
StoryImages 3

Setup built around the part

Overview AI launched OV Spark and Spark Pro on October 6 with Sparky, an assistant for choosing inspection tools and explaining results in English. Ten tools cover tasks such as counting, OCR, segmentation, anomaly detection, measurement and barcodes. Alignment makes inspection regions follow a shifting or rotating part, and an absent part causes capture failure rather than an empty-frame pass.

On-camera operation

Spark provides 1.2-megapixel imaging and Pro provides 5 megapixels, using Qualcomm Dragonwing processing in a 70 × 116 × 53 mm IP66-rated body. Model training, inference, the operator interface and PLC communication run on the device. The product documentation says production inspection and Sparky do not require cloud connectivity, while optional Defect Studio synthetic-image generation uses the cloud.

Early factory use and validation

Mansfield Engineered Components uses the camera at an end-of-line station previously checked visually, where a missing washer is a frequent defect. The products are available directly and through partners. Users still need to train applicable tools and validate lighting, cycle time and result integration. Product documentation also excludes instance segmentation for separating overlapping objects and judging them individually.
